newsitem.title: MEXICO: Early Mexico railway takeover unlikely - companies.
newsitem.headline: Early Mexico railway takeover unlikely - companies.

text.p: Officials from Mexican shipping company Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and Kansas City Southern Industries (KCSI) said on Wednesday that plans to take over their jointly owned Mexican railway by May 15 was "wishful thinking."
The recently privatized railway is still held by the Mexican government.

The two companies jointly hold the concession for the Northeast Railway, in a venture called Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM). The government will maintain a 33.5 percent stake in the railway's assets.
"We're going to try to take over as soon as possible and before the deadline of July 30, but a May 15 date is wishful thinking," TMM spokesman Fernando Ruiz told Reuters.
Mike Haverty, president of KSCI subsidiary Kansas City Southern Railway, told reporters earlier this month that TFM planned to begin operations of the railway on May 15.
"It's not going to start on May 15, probably not before July," KCSI spokesman Bill Gallagher said.
The spokesmen said start-up arrangements have been more complicated than expected.

"One of the things to be set up is the computer system for all the billing, all car counting. Also it's been a lot of work putting together the marketing and operating plan, and it will be an even greater effort to put it in to effect," Gallagher said.
Mexico's Northeast Railway, dubbed the Nafta Railroad by TFM, links Mexico City, Monterrey and Nuevo Laredo on the U.S. border, where the route connects with KSCI's railway through to Canada.
